Turn the power back on at the main power supply. <PIC> <PIC> <PIC> <PIC> , ["Manual24_54", "Manual24_55", "Manual24_56", "Manual24_57"]

question: "How can you set the PCI Express 3.0 x16 slots of a motherboard?"
ret: To set the PCI Express 3.0 x16 slots on this motherboard, you can configure their link speed via BIOS settings. Under 'PEG Port Configuration' or 'PCI Express Configuration', locate the option for 'PCIEx16_1 / PCIEx16_2 Link Speed' or 'PCIe Speed', and select the desired generation: [Auto], [Gen1], [Gen2], or [Gen3] <PIC>. For optimal graphics performance in single VGA card mode, use the PCIe 3.0 x16_1 slot (gray). Ensure the graphics card is fully seated and secured, then install appropriate drivers after booting into the OS. Refer to Chapter 2 of the manual for BIOS setup details. , ["Manual25_1"]

question: "How can you set the jumpers of a motherboard?"
ret: The motherboard manual includes descriptions of jumpers, such as the Clear RTC RAM (CLRTC) jumper and the CPU Over Voltage (CPU_OV) jumper. For example, to clear RTC RAM, you short the two pins of the CLRTC header (as shown in the manual). For CPU overclocking, the CPU_OV jumper has three pins: placing the cap on pins 1–2 restores default voltage, while placing it on pins 2–3 increases CPU voltage. Detailed jumper configurations and illustrations are provided in the motherboard manual — refer to Chapter 1.6 'Jumpers' and associated diagrams <PIC>. For precise instructions matching your specific model, consult the official manual included with your product or download the latest version from the manufacturer's website. , ["Manual25_1"]

question: "How can you set the rear panel connectors of a motherboard?"
ret: The rear panel connectors on a motherboard are pre-mounted and fixed during manufacturing—they are not user-configurable or 'set' via jumpers, BIOS, or software. As shown in the documentation, these include the PS/2 Mouse/Keyboard combo port, DisplayPort, and VGA port. They are designed to align with cutouts in the chassis rear I/O shield when the motherboard is correctly installed (edge with external ports facing the rear of the chassis). No user configuration or setting is required for these connectors. <PIC> , ["Manual25_6"]

question: "How can you set the onboard LED of a motherboard?"
ret: The onboard LED on this motherboard includes several types: the Standby Power LED (SB_PWR), Model Name LEDs, and SupremeFX LED. The Standby Power LED is hardware-controlled and cannot be configured—it lights up automatically when the system is ON, in sleep mode, or in soft-off mode. For the Model Name LEDs and SupremeFX LED, you can adjust their behavior (e.g., disable, set to Still Mode, Breathing Mode, or Flowing Mode) via BIOS or the LED Control app in Ai Suite 3. In BIOS, navigate to Advanced > Onboard Devices Configuration, then select 'Model Name LED Lighting' or 'SupremeFX LED Lighting'. <PIC> , ["Manual25_6"]

question: "How can you update the BIOS file of a motherboard?"
ret: You can update the BIOS file of a motherboard using one of the following supported methods: 1. **Via USB**: Insert a FAT32/16-formatted USB flash drive containing the latest BIOS file into a USB port; enter the BIOS setup, go to the Tool menu, select EZ Flash 3 Utility <PIC>, press <Tab> to switch to the Drive field, navigate to the USB device, then switch to Folder Info and select the BIOS file to begin the update. 2. **Via the Internet**: In EZ Flash 3, select 'by Internet', choose an Internet connection method using the arrow keys, and follow the onscreen instructions. 3. **Using BIOS Updater in FreeDOS**: Boot from the Support DVD or USB drive into FreeDOS; at the prompt, type 'd:' to access the USB drive (if applicable), then run 'bupdater /pc /g'; use <Tab> to navigate between Drives and Files panels, select the BIOS file, confirm with 'Yes', and restart after completion <PIC>. Always ensure the system is not powered off or reset during the update — doing so may cause boot failure <PIC>. , ["drill0_04", "drill0_05", "drill0_06"]

question: "How can you create RAID of a motherboard?"
ret: To create RAID on the motherboard: 1. Ensure your HDDs are connected to Intel SATA 6.0 Gb/s connectors and have no existing RAID volumes. 2. Enter BIOS and set SATA Mode to [RAID] (not the default [AHCI]). 3. Press <F11> or click the EZ Tuning Wizard icon to launch it. 4. Click RAID, then click Yes to enable RAID. 5. Select your desired RAID type: Easy Backup (RAID1 or RAID10) or Super Speed (RAID0 or RAID5). Note: RAID10 requires four HDDs. 6. Click Next, then Yes to confirm and proceed with setup. 7. After completion, click Yes to exit and OK to reset the system. For full details, refer to the manual bundled in the motherboard Support DVD. <PIC> , ["Manual25_6"]

question: "How can you use SATA ODD & USB devices to install an operating system for a motherboard?"
ret: To install an operating system (e.g., Windows 7) on a 100-series motherboard using SATA ODD and USB devices: 1. Prepare a Windows 7 installation source — either insert the OS 7 DVD into a USB ODD, or copy all files from the OS 7 DVD to a USB storage device (≥8 GB, formatted beforehand). 2. Connect the USB ODD or USB storage device to your 100-series platform. 3. Insert the motherboard's Support DVD into a SATA ODD on the same platform. 4. Power on the system and press F8 during POST to enter the boot menu <PIC>. 5. Select the USB device or SATA ODD as the boot device. 6. The USB 3.0 driver from the Support DVD will load automatically during startup — the 'Setup is starting...' screen confirms successful loading <PIC>. 7. Follow onscreen instructions to complete the OS installation. , ["boot_menu_f8", "setup_starting_screen"]

question: "How can you secure the motherboard to the chassis?"
ret: To secure the motherboard to the chassis, place it in the correct orientation—ensuring the edge with external ports aligns with the rear of the chassis <PIC>. Then, insert nine screws into the screw holes indicated by circles on the chassis/motherboard. Do not over tighten the screws, as this may damage the motherboard. , ["Manual25_6"]

question: "How can you prepare the installation of Central Processing Unit (CPU) for a motherboard?"
ret: To prepare the installation of the CPU for a motherboard: • Ensure the CPU is firmly clicked into place before installing it onto the CPU socket on the motherboard. • Use only the CPU Installation Tool for installing the CPU — do not damage or bend the tool. • Always firmly hold both sides of the CPU Installation Tool when installing, removing, or picking up the CPU. • Apply Thermal Interface Material to the CPU heatsink and CPU before installing the heatsink and fan assembly, if necessary. <PIC> , ["Manual25_11"]

question: "How do you know about system memory of a motherboard?"
ret: To know about the system memory of this motherboard: 1. It has four 288-pin DDR4 DIMM sockets, supporting unbuffered non-ECC DDR4 modules (2 GB, 4 GB, 8 GB, or 16 GB per module) <PIC>. 2. DDR4 modules are physically distinct — do NOT install DDR, DDR2, or DDR3 modules into DDR4 slots. 3. Recommended DIMM voltage is below 1.65 V to protect the CPU. 4. For optimal stability and performance, use matched 2-DIMM or 4-DIMM kits; full DIMM support depends on CPU and memory characteristics. 5. Dual-channel mode is enabled when identical sizes are installed in Channel A and B; mismatched sizes result in partial dual-channel + single-channel operation. 6. Memory compatibility is validated via the motherboard’s Qualified Vendors List (QVL), supporting DDR4 speeds up to 3400 MHz (overclocked) <PIC>. 7. Note: On 32-bit OS, usable memory may be limited to ~3 GB or less even with ≥4 GB installed. , ["motherboard_memory_qvl_3400", "motherboard_ddr4_socket_diagram"]

question: "How do you know about Serial port connector (10-1 pin COM) of a motherboard?"
ret: The 10-1 pin Serial Port (COM) connector on the motherboard is used to connect a serial port module cable. After connecting the cable to this header, the COM module must be installed into a slot opening at the rear of the system chassis. Note that the COM module is purchased separately. In BIOS, you can configure the serial port via 'Serial Port [On/Off]' and adjust its base I/O address and IRQ settings (e.g., IO=3F8h; IRQ=4) under 'Serial Port Configuration'. <PIC> , ["Manual25_6"]

question: "How do you know about TPM connector (14-1 pin TPM) for a motherboard?"
ret: The TPM connector (14-1 pin TPM) is an internal motherboard header designed to support a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) system. It enables secure storage of cryptographic keys, digital certificates, passwords, and sensitive data. Additionally, a TPM system helps enhance network security, protect digital identities, and ensure platform integrity. <PIC> , ["Manual25_1"]

question: "How do you know about Thermal sensor connector (2-pin T_SENSOR) of a motherboard?"
ret: The Thermal sensor connector (2-pin T_SENSOR) is a dedicated header on the motherboard designed for connecting a thermistor cable. It enables monitoring of temperature from critical components or external devices. The T_Sensor temperature is displayed in the BIOS Monitor menu (under 'T_Sensor Temperature') and can be selected as a temperature source for fan control (e.g., in Q-Fan Configuration for Extension or Chassis Fans). <PIC> , ["Manual25_1"]

question: "How can you set quick release for a multi-use pressure cooker and air fryer?"
ret: To set Quick Release for your multi-use pressure cooker and air fryer: Press the quick release button down until it clicks and locks into the Vent position. A jet of steam will eject through the top of the steam release valve — this is normal.
